name: disclosure
title: Disclosure
purpose: A native details element that shows or hides detail under a summary written in text.
whenToUse: For detail most readers can do without: a log, the environment, the steps of a finished attempt.
With the row variant inside a list row, for a changed file that opens to its diff. The summary holds the path and the counts.
For the one group of advanced settings in a view. Mark that details element with data-ds-advanced.
whenNotToUse: For anything the reader must see or do in order to go on. An action marked data-ds-critical that can be reached only inside closed content fails the hidden-critical-action rule: show it in the view too, or open the disclosure by default.
Nested more than two levels. A third level fails the disclosure-depth rule: move that content to a view of its own.
With a summary that is only an icon or is empty. A summary without text fails the summary-without-text rule.
For a list of actions that opens over the page. Use a menu.
For sections where opening one must close the others. This component has no script, so each disclosure opens and closes alone.

variants.name: default
variants.use: Stands alone. Its content is indented to start under the summary's text.

variants.name: row
variants.use: The only child of a ds-list__row. The summary is the row, and the content uses the row's full width, which a diff needs at phone width.

sizes.name: default
sizes.use: The summary is at least 44px tall and as wide as the disclosure. It grows when its text wraps.

accessibility: Use a details element with a summary as its first child. The browser gives the summary its role and its expanded state, and the open attribute is the only state: never toggle a class.
The summary holds text that says what is inside. The chevron is drawn by the stylesheet and needs no markup. Do not put a heading, a button or a link inside the summary.

Trailing text such as a count goes in a ds-disclosure__meta span inside the summary, after the label. It is read as part of the summary's name, so write counts in words or with a hidden label, as ds-diff__counts does.
Put the content in one ds-disclosure__content element after the summary.

Tab reaches the summary. Enter and Space open and close it. Both come from the summary element. Closed content is out of the tab order and is skipped by a screen reader, and the browser's find-in-page opens it.
Set the open attribute in markup to start open. Start open when the content holds an action the reader needs.
Fetch heavy content, such as a diff, when the disclosure opens, and show the content's own loading state until it arrives.
